With a controller, use Rearrange this tab. releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7.2
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7.2 ## New - **ZeroFG frame generation:** (experimental) adds frames between the ones a game draws, x2, x3 or x4, up to your display's refresh rate. It's in Settings > Performance and in the in-game menu. Switch it on before starting a game, switched on during one, it starts after Apply & Restart. By @hy300leosquizz-ctrl (#331).

releases.name: ARMSX3 for iOS 0.0.4 beta
releases.body:
## Graphics and memory

**Faster frame submission.** MoltenVK now turns each frame into Metal work on its own thread instead of on the graphics thread, so the graphics thread spends almost no time submitting a frame. Framebuffers are now freed only after the GPU has finished with them, which this needed. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Freed textures give their memory back.** Large texture allocations now get memory of their own, which goes back to iOS when the texture is freed. Before, one texture still in use kept a whole 64 MB block, and One Piece held 2.3 GB of blocks for 643 MB of textures. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Upload buffer space comes back sooner.** The texture upload buffer gives back finished space after every full GPU wait, where it held it until the next frame and swapped in a new buffer instead.

**No stall on the first new shader.** The shader compiler's one-time setup now happens at boot. It used to land in gameplay, on the first shader a game hadn't shown before. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Black Ops II weapon.** The weapon in your hands no longer draws with its triangles over each other.

releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7.1
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7.1 ## Games - **Uncharted 2: Among Thieves, Super Street Fighter IV, Journey, and other games:** fixed the stop with "Failed to compile fragment shader" at the default Shader Precision (Low). - **Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction:** fixed the freeze on Cobalia (thanks Seeslo for testing). -**Uncharted 3: Drake’s Deception** gets The Last of Us fix for freezes during play, since both games run the same job system, prevents freezes in UC3. ## Save states - **Save states from 1.7 and earlier don't load in 1.7.1,** because RPCS3's font module update changed the save state format. In-game saves are not affected.

releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7 ## Highlights - **New SPU code compiles in the background.** Games keep running while it compiles, so new areas load without pausing. Games that need the old pause keep it. - **Compiled SPU code now carries over between updates,** including game updates, so first boots after them are quick. Each game compiles once more on its first boot after this update. ## The Last of Us - **Fixed the freeze during play.** The game hands its work to background jobs and waits for them, and on phones a job list could stop with work still in it, freezing the game anywhere from minutes to hours in. ARMSX3 now keeps those jobs moving.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.9
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.9 gives the Commander X16's network card Zimodem's command-mode connections, so programs that open several connections at once, like Veranda's Gemini, Gopher, FTP and chat programs, now connect.

## What's new

- **Veranda's network programs connect.** The X16's network card now handles the Zimodem commands that [Veranda](https://github.com/veranda-x16/veranda) uses to keep several connections open at once. Its Gemini browser, Gopher client, FTP and chat programs can reach the internet from the emulator.
- **Secure connections.** Programs can now open encrypted (TLS) connections through the X16's network card, which Gemini and HTTPS need. As on the real card, the card does the encryption itself and doesn't check the server's certificate.

## Downloads

| macOS, Apple Silicon   | `_aarch64.dmg`              |
| macOS, Intel           | `_x64.dmg`                  |

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.8
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.8 brings the Apple II to phones and tablets, turns the touch screen into the Commander X16's mouse and the NES Zapper, and fixes the picture being cut off on phones with a gesture bar.

## What's new

- **The Apple II on a phone or tablet.** Hold it upright for a keyboard: Android's own, with rows of Esc, Tab, Ctrl, the arrows and Delete above it, plus Open Apple and Closed Apple, which stay down while you touch them. Reset only presses once you've held it for half a second, so a stray tap won't reset the machine. Turn it sideways for a joystick: an analog stick that moves as far as you push it, and buttons 0 and 1. Move it, resize it or hide it from the pause menu, as with the other pads.
- **The touch screen is the X16's mouse.** Drag a finger on the picture to move the pointer, tap to click, tap with two fingers to right-click, and tap then hold to drag. It works in the app and in the browser, so mouse programs like the Veranda desktop work on a phone.
- **Tap to shoot with the Zapper.** In Zapper games like Duck Hunt, tap the picture where you want to shoot.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.7
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.7 brings the Commander X16 to phones and tablets, with a keyboard in portrait and a SNES pad in landscape, gives the X16 all its function keys and proper SNES controllers everywhere, and tidies up Android.

## What's new

- **The X16 on a phone or tablet.** Hold it upright for a keyboard: Android's own, with autocorrect and suggestions off, and rows of Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, the arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down and Delete/Insert above it. Ctrl and Alt are sticky, so Ctrl then C sends Ctrl+C; tap twice to hold them. Fn brings up F1 to F12. Turn it sideways for a SNES pad.
- **Hide controls.** The pause menu on a touch screen can hide the on-screen controls for the rest of the game, and show them again.
- **The X16's F-keys are its own.** On the X16, and on the other computers that use the whole keyboard (Skink and BASIC), F1 to F12 go to the machine, so programs like busterm get them all. Open Bus's own keys move behind Ctrl+Shift: Ctrl+Shift+F1 opens the menu, Ctrl+Shift+F2 saves a state, and so on.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.6
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.6 lets you install the web version as an app that opens without the internet, and fixes a way to get stuck in a game on Android phones.

## What's new

- **Install the web version as an app.** At https://obus.tuxprint.com/, Chrome and Edge offer to install Open Bus with its own window and icon, and Settings → Library has an Install button where your browser supports it. On iPhone, use Share → Add to Home Screen.
- **The web version works offline.** Once it's been opened, it opens again with no internet connection. It still picks up updates whenever you're online.
- **Your games stay put in the browser.** When you first add a game, the page asks the browser not to clear your games when it runs low on space.

## Fixed

- **Stuck in the emulator's menu on an Android phone.** Pressing Select and Start together on the on-screen controls opened a menu the on-screen buttons couldn't work, so the only way out was to quit the game. On-screen Select and Start now go to the game. A gamepad's Select and Start still open the menu, and Back still pauses.

## Downloads

| System                 | File                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------- |

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.5
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.5 makes the Android app work on phones and tablets, with on-screen controls for NES games, and keeps the Commander X16's clock on time.

## What's new

- **On-screen controls for NES games** on a phone or tablet with no gamepad: a D-pad, A and B, Select and Start. They hide when a gamepad connects and come back when it disconnects.
- **Move controls.** Drag each piece where you want it, make them bigger or smaller, turn the vibration off, or put B higher than A. Your layout is kept.
- **A pause menu for touch screens.** Back opens it: Resume, Save state, Load state, Reset, Move controls and Quit. Before this, there was no way out of a game on a phone without a gamepad.
- **The library on phones** stays clear of the status bar, navigation bar, camera cutout and on-screen keyboard. Games are always fullscreen.
- **The sidebar with a gamepad.** On a phone, opening the sidebar moves the gamepad's selection into it.

## Fixed

- **A TV remote's OK** stopped choosing in the menus if you bound A to something else, and didn't work in the X16's menu at all. It now always works in the menus, whatever the controls are set to.

New audio, rendering, and Android startup fixes are here. Huge thanks to
[Andrew Nakas](https://github.com/andrewnakas) and contributors for the underlying
work, and [AlanConstantino](https://github.com/AlanConstantino) for integrating
it and testing on Retroid Pocket 6 in [PR #123](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/pull/123).
Alex McHugh's Skate3Recomp and ReXGlue/Xenia remain the foundation of this port.

## Download

Most players want **Skate3-Mobile-Android.apk**. Install over your existing
main app. Do not uninstall first. Android will ask you to approve the update.
Your extracted game files stay in place.

[Download the main APK](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/releases/download/v2.1.0/Skate3-Mobile-Android.apk)
or [get the separate QA Build](https://github.com/Buku313/Skate3-Mobile/releases/download/v2.1.0-qa1/Skate3-Mobile-QA.apk).
The debug APK is for users of the separate developer app.

Older QA and developer builds used the main app's update address. Install the
matching v2.1 APK once, without uninstalling. From this version onward, each
app receives updates for its own package only.

## What changed

releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 6

This QA build targets an intermittent early-boot hang reported on the Retroid Pocket 5.

The failed QA 5 diagnostic showed a live audio thread but no first presentation, native pipeline creation, scene target, or crash. The guest render thread stopped immediately after its first offscreen 2D captures.

QA 6 tightens the boot capture boundary:

- Only the four verified 2D vertex layouts and three supported primitive types are accepted.
- Individual and per-frame 2D payloads have conservative size limits.
- Invalid transient draw state is rejected before reading guest memory.
- The first twelve guest frames now log capture begin and completion markers.

Install QA 6 over the previous QA app, keep the System Driver selected, fully close the app between attempts, and test at least five launches. Attach diagnostics from any failed launch.

The stable app and stable update channel are unchanged. The APK includes no game data.

releases.name: Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5
releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5

This is an opt-in diagnostic build that installs over earlier **Skate 3 QA** builds and preserves QA app data.

## RP5 intermittent black-screen fix

QA 4 proved that the Retroid Pocket 5 can render the Quality profile's 1280x720 scene target, but testers reported that startup only succeeded roughly half the time.

The QA 4 profile copied Performance's visible feature settings, but one internal pipeline gate still used the profile number. Quality therefore compiled optional outline, spline, and shadow shader families even though those features were disabled. Cold and partially warmed shader caches could take different startup paths.

QA 5 fixes the mismatch:

- The 1280x720 Quality target remains enabled.
- The pipeline builder now follows the active lean-scene flag instead of assuming every Quality profile needs the full optional PSO set.
- Renderer installation applies the same defensive lean-feature guard.
- The startup log must report `lean Android set` for this QA Quality profile.
- Stable v2.0.17 and its update channel remain unchanged.

## RP5 test

1. Install QA 5 directly over QA 4.
2. Keep the System Driver selected.

# 0.60.1 is out

There was a bug in the AppImage Updater Code. To fix this i have to revert to the old AppImage build and wait several weeks to ensure a smooth update process.

# 0.60.0 is out 🎉

This release is special for me. I build emuze with web technologies because that’s where I have the most experience, and I’m really proud of what I’ve achieved over the years. I’ve always wanted to help out in this wonderful emulation community, but aside from testing, I couldn’t do much to help with the emulators I love because I struggled with C++ code, which most emulators are written in. But sometimes you feel forced to try and try again. Since v0.59.0, I’ve successfully added a [change to RMG](https://github.com/Rosalie241/RMG/pull/518) to use the SDL GUID to identify a gamepad more reliably, and I forked Mednafen with [mednafen-sdl3](https://github.com/bmsuseluda/mednafen-sdl3) to greatly expand gamepad support. Those changes are just baby steps in the grand scheme of things, but they felt great, and I hope I can build on them in the future.

# 0.59.2 is out 🎉

This release is mostly preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0.
Besides this fuse2 is not necessary anymore and Metainfos for AppImage Managers e.g. AM are included.

Please let me know what you think of it in the [emuze discord](https://discord.gg/tCzK7kc6Y4).

## 💥 Features
- added AppImage Metainfos
- AppImage works without fuse2
- Preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0

# 0.59.0 is out 🎉

As you might now i love the simplicity of console gaming. You start the game and it just works. With emulation more often then not you have to provide more then just the game. You need things like a BIOS file, firmware or key files. I wanted to assist with this for a long time. With this release you can choose a folder where you can put your BIOS files and emuze will pick them up and configure the Emulators. Of course emuze will tell you if a required file is missing. On top of this emuze comes bundled with open source BIOS implementations for PlayStation, Game Boy Advance and NEO GEO. Of course you can use official BIOS files instead if you need by putting them in the BIOS folder. Sadly i was not able to achieve the same result for more complicated systems like PlayStation 3, WiiU and Switch. These systems require a installation of a firmware. I will try to tackle these in a future release.

Besides this i bundled and pre configured ScummVM and DOSBox Pure Unleashed.
Therefore the day is finally here: All 35 supported systems are pre configured and bundled now 🥳

# 0.58.0 is out 🎉

As one of the few nerdy kids in a small sleepy town in a country where arcade gaming was classified as gambling i could see lightgun games in magazines only. I had an NES and Captain N with his Zapper was sooo awesome to me. But when the time came that i could buy one with my own money the rise of flat panels began and with it the death of CRT TVs and Lightguns altogether. It was just a thing of the past, sadly.
But surprisingly the genre came back with the Wii and PS3 and there Pointer devices. Some years later camera based Lightguns came to the market and finally Lightgun gaming with the same and even higher precision is possible on flat panels.

## Endemic life is visible

Small creatures in the field (Stinkmink, Clothfly and the rest of the endemic life) were invisible in the port: you could still pick them up and get their buffs, but nothing was drawn. The game decides whether to draw them from a visibility test it runs on the GPU and then reads back on the CPU; the port never copied that result back, so the game always read "not visible". Now it does. Only that small result is copied, so the frame rate stays at a locked 30 fps.

- An empty file `sin_devolver_copias` in the game folder brings back the old behaviour.

Thanks to the player who reported it in issue #8.

Nothing else changes: shader caches are the same as in 1.6.0, so your existing caches keep working.

releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

The headline is that the hybrid JIT now translates **more than 80 % of the guest instruction
stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

| Windows x64 | `Model3-Vulkan.v0.9.9.8.for.Windows.zip` | Windows 10/11, Vulkan 1.3 |

**Windows only.** This release contains a single asset for Windows x64. Everything else is
v0.9.8.6 unchanged.

## Why the v0.9.8.6 Windows package refused to start on AMD graphics cards

On Windows, AMD's Vulkan driver reports **128 bytes** of push constants — the amount Vulkan itself
guarantees. Every driver this renderer had been developed against reports 256.

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

The headline is that the hybrid JIT now translates **more than 80 % of the guest instruction
stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. It is built from source and is not in the release archives. See [the libretro page](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro.md) and [the Mac guide](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro_macos.md).

- **Faster catch-up** when you start watching a live match partway through.

releases.name: SameBoy v1.0.5
releases.body:
This version is backwards compatible with save states from SameBoy 0.14.3 and newer, as well as save states from any BESS compliant emulator

## New/Improved Features
* Better ZIP file compatibility in iOS
* Added keyboard shortcuts for the VRAM and Memory Viewers in the Cocoa frontends
  * VRAM Viewer tabs can be switched using ^1 - ^4
* `0x` can now be used an an alternative hexadecimal prefix in the debugger and Memory Viewer

## Accuracy Improvements/Fixes
* More accurate emulation of invalid MLT_REQ SGB commands
* Fixed a bug where certain Game Boy Printer margin configurations were not emulated correctly
* When emulating an RTC cartridge in Sync-to-Host mode, the RTC will now correctly halt if instructed by the ROM
* Improved Game Boy Printer accuracy and timings
* More realistic IR emulation, fixes IR features in certain games
* Improved DAC emulation, especially on pre-GBC models
* Improved LFSR stepping on pre-GBC models
* Emulate a quirk where square channels keep running "in the background" after their timer expired on pre-GBC models
* On pre-GBC models, the duty cycle of square channels is now latched between frequency clocks

releases.name: SameBoy v1.0.4
releases.body:
This version is backwards compatible with save states from SameBoy 0.14.3 and newer, as well as save states from any BESS compliant emulator

## New/Improved Features
* The libretro core now supports API extensions to retrieve additional metadata and create more portable battery save files
* The iOS frontend has been updated with improved iOS 27 support
* iPhone Duo support was added to the iOS frontend
* The CRT scaling filter has been updated with an improved look
* A new Pixelated/Sharp Bilinear scaling filter
    * This new filter is now the default filter in the Cocoa and SDL frontends
* VFS support was added to the libretro core
* Logging support was added to the libretro core
* The libretro core will now render audio directly in the frontend's audio sample rate, if supported
* Recording audio to a VGM log file is now possible in the Cocoa and SDL frontends
* Minor UI improvements in the Cocoa frontend

## Accuracy Improvements/Fixes

releases.name: XRecomp v0.19.0
releases.body:
# XRecomp 0.19.0

<!-- Highlights: what changed, what works, known problems. Written by hand, kept across updates. -->

A second Xbox 360 performance night, measured headless on Warhammer: Battle March. Frames and save states are byte
identical to 0.18.0, except where a change is opt-in or per title (below).

- **Guest CPU**: `MmQueryStatistics` keeps a page count instead of scanning (it was half of the boot's host CPU). The
  VMX helpers work on 16- and 8-bit lanes, use the compiler's vector extensions and are inlined. Host CPU: the boot
  is 3× faster and in-game play 1.8× (141 → 79 ms of guest time per swap). The scheduler turn is cheaper and makes
  the same decisions. Prepare is not slower: the VMX-heavy files compile 27–41 % faster with NDK clang.
- **Renderer**: 16-bit resolve formats take the fast path, and the stencil is read back in 2 passes instead of 8.
  Tiled addressing is worked out per tile row, texture rows are read 16 bytes at a time, texture memory is hashed in
  8 lanes and packed vertex formats use tables. Renderer CPU per swap is about half of 0.18.0's.

releases.body:
# XRecomp 0.18.0

<!-- Highlights: what changed, what works, known problems. Written by hand, kept across updates. -->

A speed night on every console but the Xbox 360. Every change is bit-exact: frame, RAM and audio hashes over 600
frames or more are identical to 0.17.0, and lockstep with the interpreters holds.

| Console | x86-64 instructions per frame (bench) | Prepare again? |
|---|---|---|
| GBA | 9.06M → 7.09M (−22 %) | yes |
| PS1 | 8.08M → 6.49M (−20 %) | no |
| N64 | 6.58M → 5.65M (−14 %) | yes |
| GameCube | audio mix −24 %, GX front end −14 % | no |
| Xbox | float stack code −30 % on arm64 (`fistp` without libm) | yes |

- **GBA**: the prefetch model charges a run of plain instructions in one call, and exact segment cycles keep lifted
  code running (instructions handed to the interpreter −43 %).
- **PS1**: the SPU skips idle voices and silent reverb; handed instructions run in one loop; the HLE interrupt entry
  and exit copy registers in blocks.
- **N64**: COUNT reads stay in lifted code (polling screens 7× cheaper); one range test per store; the AI resampler
  skips silence; a cheaper dispatcher hit.

releases.name: Zaxnes 0.6.0
releases.body:
This one is mostly about what happens *under* the 3D. The emulator itself got a lot better.

## New

**Accuracy: 147 of 147 on AccuracyCoin.** 0.5.0 passed 128. Zaxnes was also compared cycle by cycle with a transistor-level simulation of the NES chips (421,901 CPU cycles, DMA included), and the timing matched. Where the two still differ, tests made on real consoles side with Zaxnes.

**Over 400 mappers.** Up from 144. That includes the **Famicom Disk System**, the **VS. System** with its cabinet buttons, and newer boards like the Rainbow.

**A fast core.** It skips work the screen doesn't need, but gives the same results as the accurate core. We checked that frame by frame on 320 ROMs. Handhelds use it by default.

**New options window.** One slider goes from *Fastest* to *Most faithful* and sets everything that costs speed. A simple mode shows only what most people need, and an advanced mode shows everything. It works the same on the PC and on the console screen.

releases.name: Zaxnes 0.5.0
releases.body:
Zaxnes is an independent project, not affiliated with Geod Studio or Nintendo.

## Highlights

**3dSen 2.0 and 2.1 compatibility.** Profiles from 3dSen 2.0 and 2.1 import and play, with what the new versions brought: reflections, bend, the new camera and Lua features.

**A real NES emulator, not just a gimmick.** Mapper support goes from 85 to 144, and AccuracyCoin from 89 to 128 tests out of 147. More accuracy work is coming in the next releases.

**New widescreen hacks: Kirby's Adventure and Faxanadu.** Every regional version of each. Faxanadu already has its 3D profile in this release; Kirby's is on the way.

**Smooth scrolling at 120 Hz (experimental).** On a 120 Hz screen, the playfield is drawn between two emulated frames, from the run-ahead.

**RetroArch shaders.** Slang shaders (through librashader) on the Vulkan / DirectX 12 renderer: CRT, scanlines, LCD, Mega Bezel TV frames. A pack of presets is built in, separately for 2D and 3D. Available on Android too.

**Editor mode for 3D profiles (work in progress).** An AI-assisted editor: it gives an AI agent a harness through a local MCP server, and a prompt ready to copy and paste. Expect more on it in the next release.

> ⚠️ The game is not included — you need your own legally obtained, **decrypted** PS5 dump (PPSA29802).

### Fixes
- **A second player (2P) joined when pausing.** The game opens a second ("special") pad port, and it got the same input as the real pad, so Options there counted as player 2 joining. Only the standard port is the pad now.
- **Touches beside the on-screen buttons acted as a mouse**, a second input device for the game. The touch controls are the only player-1 input now (a real mouse or keyboard still works once used).

### Performance and heat
- **Built-in Turnip updated to Mesa 26.3** with our patch for importing the game's memory directly (no per-draw copies). If you picked another driver in *Settings → GPU driver*, switch back to **Built-in**: drivers without this import copy memory on every draw.

releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **How far this was tested.** This is 1.0 plus one fix, built and checked on a PC. The fix has not been played on an affected phone yet. Please report problems with a debug report (☰ → Bug reports → Make a debug report).

Install it over 1.0 or older. Your saves, settings and setup stay. **No new setup is needed**: just press Play. The first start after updating takes a little longer while the graphics pipelines are rebuilt once.

Everything here applies to both Pokémon Sword and Pokémon Shield (update 1.3.2).

---

## Fixed in 1.01

- **Missing ground on some Snapdragon phones.** On phones with Qualcomm's older graphics driver (for example a Xiaomi 12, Snapdragon 8 Gen 1), parts of the field were not drawn: the sky showed through the ground and cliffs. The Mali white-screen fix from v0.97 changed how these phones read some of the game's model data, which their driver did not handle. It now applies to Mali phones only, where it is needed.

## From 1.0

- Less work for the GPU per frame, a crash risk removed, and new timing tools. Full notes: the [1.0 release](https://github.com/simipoB/Galar-Native-Android/releases/tag/v1.0).

## Known problems

releases.name: Galar Native 1.0
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **How far this was tested.** Everything new in 1.0 was built and checked on a PC (including simulated Mali, Adreno, Xclipse and PowerVR GPUs), but has not been played on a phone yet. Expect problems, and please report them with a debug report (☰ → Bug reports → Make a debug report).

Install it over v0.99 or older. Your saves, settings and setup stay. **No new setup is needed**: just press Play.

Everything here applies to both Pokémon Sword and Pokémon Shield (update 1.3.2).

---

## New in 1.0

- **Less work for the GPU**: fewer drawing passes per frame (clears are folded into the next pass, empty depth passes are gone) and depth and stencil that a pass does not change are no longer written back to memory. This helps most on Mali and older Adreno phones. If objects go missing or flicker after updating, add `DM_VK_LAZY_CLEAR=0` to env.txt and tell us in an issue.
- **A crash risk removed**: a diagnostic that sampled the game during loads could, rarely, break the game's own code at that moment. It is now off and made safe (it closed Legends: Arceus at start in v0.99).

releases.name: Galar Native v0.99
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **How far this was tested.** An earlier build of the speed work below was played on a Galaxy S25+ (shorter wait before play, less memory, a steady 30). The last part of it (how the game and the graphics wait for each other) and the new setup and Players screens were built and checked on a PC only. Expect problems, and please report them (see the end of these notes). The Mali changes from v0.97 have still not been played on a Mali phone.

Install it over v0.98, v0.97 or v0.96. Your saves, settings and setup stay. **No new setup is needed**: just press Play.

Everything here applies to both Pokémon Sword and Pokémon Shield (one app runs both, update 1.3.2).

---

## Faster

- **Almost no wait after Play.** The shaders the game needs are ready from the last time you played, so the game starts at once (on the S25+: from about 1.5 s to 0.1 s, and none from the second start on).
- **Shorter loading screens and steadier frames.** The game and the graphics no longer wait for each other longer than they need to, so frames reach the screen sooner and loading screens no longer wait for the screen's refresh on every frame.

releases.name: Galar Native v0.98
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **How far this was tested.** The memory fix and the other fixes below were built and checked on a PC; they have not been played on a phone yet. The Mali changes from v0.97 (Faster rendering on Mali, less work per object on most G615 phones) have also not been played on a Mali phone yet. Please report problems (see the end of these notes).

Install it over v0.97 or v0.96. Your saves, settings and setup stay. **No new setup is needed**: just press Play.

Everything here applies to both Pokémon Sword and Pokémon Shield (one app runs both, update 1.3.2).

---

## The Dynamax crash and the crash when changing your lead Pokémon

- **The game no longer closes when one of its memory areas runs out.** Sword and Shield keep fixed-size memory areas for things like effects, textures and lists. On Android some of them filled up, and the game then used memory it never got and closed. That was the Dynamax crash, the crash when changing the first Pokémon in your team, and several other crashes in the middle of play. When an area is full, the game now gets memory from a reserve instead. (#211, #272, #298, #330, #341, #343, #344, #345, #346)

releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **How far this was tested.** The Mali white-screen fix was tested on a POCO X6 Pro (Mali-G615 MC6, Arm's driver r44p1): Route 1 draws correctly. The Mali speed changes below were measured from that phone's logs but have not been played on a Mali phone yet. Everything was built and checked on a PC. Please report problems (see the end of these notes).

Install it over v0.96. Your saves, settings and setup stay. **No new setup is needed**: just press Play.

Everything here applies to both Pokémon Sword and Pokémon Shield (one app runs both, update 1.3.2).

---

## Mali: the white screen is fixed

- **Sword and Shield now draw correctly on Mali phones with Arm's own driver** (the phone's normal driver). The field, grass and lighting were white. The game stores some per-vertex data, such as normals and colours, as small whole numbers; Arm's driver changed those numbers before the game's shaders could read them, and the lighting came out far too bright. They now reach the shaders unchanged, as on the Switch. You no longer need the PanVK driver for this. (#215, #227, #282, #311, #316)
- If you turned on any of the menu's "White screen tests (Mali)", turn them off again.

## SkyNetEmu 0.2.4

Source revision: `c57e7f5d7608691bde97bc1c523c22ddf25604c6` (version code 7, version name `0.2.4-stable+c57e7f5`). A small update to 0.2.3.

## SkyNetEmu 0.2.2

Source revision: `48f360d1edca3859f72e447e6943a21ee8eede91` (version code 5, version name `0.2.2-stable+48f360d`).

### Fixes and improvements

**Same game presets on every phone**
- Game presets are no longer limited to particular processors, and the Snapdragon-specific BeamNG Box64 presets are gone. Every phone sees the same presets.
- Presets no longer name a GPU driver; the app picks one for your GPU:
  - Linux games get a Turnip driver when a preset is imported, when a shortcut is created and when a game starts. Adreno 735, 740 and 750 get Mesa Turnip 26.2.2; Adreno 730 gets Turnip v27.0.0 r6; Adreno 8xx keeps its current driver.
  - Windows games get the driver mapped to your GPU when they start, or the system driver when none is mapped.

**Crashes**
- Games no longer crash with SIGSYS on Android versions whose system-call filter refuses calls FEX makes (all FEX + bionic BeamNG starts on a POCO F6 with Android 14 died this way). A refused call now fails normally and is logged to `Winlator/logs/sigsys.log`.
- BeamNG 0.34 now starts on Box64 + bionic without PRoot. It used to crash about a second after start with exit 134 (seen on a OnePlus 11).

releases.name: SkyNetEmu 0.2.1
releases.body:
## SkyNetEmu 0.2.1

Source revision: `e750c469bed4a87644a1dac43ff7e1a137d32120` (version code 4, version name `0.2.1-stable+e750c46`).

### Fixes and improvements

**Counter-Strike 2**
- CS2 starts again on a fresh install. The game stopped with "A game file appears to be missing or corrupted" because its Panorama text library could not load next to the root filesystem's newer HarfBuzz. The app now carries the six small font libraries it needs (unmodified Debian 11 builds of HarfBuzz, FriBidi, libthai, libdatrie, Graphite2 and Pixman) instead of relying on Valve's Steam Linux Runtime 3.0 (sniper) being installed.
- The menu's background videos play from a Steam library on shared storage. The x86-64 and 32-bit x86 shims were missing the `flock` fallback that the aarch64 one already had, so file locks failed on shared storage.

**BeamNG.drive**
- BeamNG 0.39 and 0.40 now offer a single preset: FEX + bionic, no PRoot, direct launch, 960x544. The Box64, Box64 bionic, SoC-specific Box64 and Windows ARM64 presets are removed from those two versions; older BeamNG versions keep theirs.

releases.name: SkyNetEmu 0.2.0

## SkyNetEmu 0.2.0

Source revision: `5e2bcd1806815831a04d18b2b843735200461d0f` (version code 3, version name `0.2.0-stable+5e2bcd1`).

### Fixes and improvements

**Linux games on Android**
- Linux games can run on the bionic FEX without PRoot (direct FEX bridge), with game profiles and presets for BeamNG.drive 0.34, 0.39 and 0.40, Shadow of the Tomb Raider, Rise of the Tomb Raider, Dead Island Definitive Edition, Alien: Isolation and Counter-Strike 2. A Box64 + bionic + no PRoot preset starts BeamNG 0.39 reliably.
- Games run directly from shared storage: FEX retries file mappings that Android's noexec storage refuses, so BeamNG no longer needs staged copies. The old staging code is removed, and its leftover files are deleted when a Linux session starts.
- Steam libraries on shared storage (`SkyNetEmu/Games`): installs work, installed games get shortcuts, and a fresh install finds games that are already downloaded there instead of offering to download them again.

## Somniel v0.1.7a

**A small update: a way to save a log of what went wrong, so crashes and loading-screen hangs can be tracked down.**

  responding (not after you simply swiped it away), it asks whether to save the log of that run to the same folder.
  Choose *Save log*; nothing is sent anywhere, the file just waits in your Downloads folder.
- The audio-failure log from v0.1.7 now goes to the same `somniel_logs` folder (it used to be `Somniel_log`).

### Bug reports
From now on **every crash or hang report needs the saved log attached** (the `.txt` from `Downloads/somniel_logs`).
Without it there is usually no way to tell what happened on a GPU we cannot test.

### Download

  room again. It never goes above your choice.

releases.name: 宝可梦传说 Z-A · Mali 零拷贝修复（3→30 FPS）
releases.body:
# 宝可梦传说 Z‑A 安卓移植 · Mali 零拷贝修复版（宿主 APK）

**这是一个“宿主”APK：只含移植运行时，不含任何游戏数据、NSO、资源或密钥。**
运行它需要你**自备自己游戏卡带/数字版的转储**，并用 [nx2android](https://github.com/shirai91/nx2android)
的 porter 生成数据包（步骤见仓库 README 的「怎么用」与「自备文件与公开性」）。

## 这版修了什么（Mali‑G925 上 3 FPS → 30 FPS）

- **根因**：MTK（MT6991）的 gralloc 给 `AHardwareBuffer` 的 native handle 有 3 个 fd，
  `fd[0]` 是 size 0 的只读元数据文件，`fd[1]` 才是 dma-buf（`st_size == 缓冲区大小`）。
  上游恒取 `fds[0]` 去 `mmap`，于是这台 Mali 上 771 MB 的 NVN 内存池**全部**退回
  “每提交整池双向 memcpy”，每帧约 375 ms——这正是帧时间的大头。
- **修法**：`ahb_buf_fd()` 按 `fstat().st_size == 池大小` 选出真正的 dma-buf fd；
  `pool_zero_copy()` 与 `vk_pool_remap_ro()` 都改用它。补丁全文：
  [`patches/nx2android/local-patches-2026-11-04.patch`](https://github.com/Timqt/pokelegza-and/blob/main/patches/nx2android/local-patches-2026-11-04.patch)
- **实测**（25079RPDCC，Dimensity 9400 级，Mali‑G925‑Immortalis MC12，Vulkan 1.3.278）：

| | 修复前 | 修复后 |
|---|---|---|
| 零拷贝内存池 | 0 / 771 MB | **771.2 / 771.2 MB** |
| 菜单 FPS | 2–3 | **30**（游戏自身 present interval 上限） |
| 帧工作 p50 | 343 ms | **16.9 ms** |
| submit+present | 53–82 ms | 3–4.5 ms |

- 已能从语言选择一路进到开场列车场景（字幕 “Your train has arrived in Lumiose
  City!”）。当前瓶颈是 GPU 渲染（场景内约 20–25 ms，≈48 FPS 上限）。

## 使用

Coffee GB 2.1.6 adds BESS save-state interchange, expands Game Boy peripheral support, and brings connection choices and device controls together in the desktop menu.

## Changes

- Load and save BESS-compatible states from the File menu, with validated ROM matching and interchange for supported DMG, CGB, and SGB configurations.
- Use HuC-1/HuC-3 cartridge infrared and send or receive GBKiss GBF files.
- Scan EAN-13 barcodes with the separate Barcode Taisen Bardigun reader.
- Run Pocket Sonar with MBC1S sensor emulation and simulated sonar input. Scene changes now end active input recording, and the mapper is included in state coverage checks.
- Use Turbo File GB internal memory and removable cards, including import/export, persistence, and write protection. The GBA-only Advance choice is no longer exposed in the menu; legacy state and storage support is retained.
- Emulate Singer and Jaguar sewing machines, including the JN-2000 embroidery arm, live stitch preview, and PNG export.
- Organize Peripherals into Link port, Cartridge, and Infrared. Device submenus combine Connect with their controls; Mobile Adapter configuration moves from Preferences into its device submenu.

**Fixed**
- **Uncharted 1 could close now and then in play.** On the Retroid Pocket G2 this happened about once in three hours without the frame rate limit. **Fixed**
- **Uncharted 3: Drake's desert clothes from chapter 16 on and the horses of chapters 19 and 20 were drawn as stretched triangles** (#35). ## Xenra 0.5.0

### A new platform: iOS

Xenra ships on iPad and iPhone for the first time, as one app with both
consoles:

  and the floating pad with physical controller support.
- Dashboard, game library with box art and covers, setup wizard, per-game

  retail dashboard, all from the app.

The iOS and Android screens share their wording and layout, so a guide written
for one applies to the other.

The Performance core is the default original Xbox core on Android, chosen per
game at launch. xemu remains for the dashboard, the Insignia setup assistant and
the games the performance core cannot run, exactly the split the game menu
already understands. The core names in the library and per-game settings are now
Performance and Compatibility, matching the 360 side.

### Mali GPUs and compatibility rendering

## Back up before upgrading

Close the game and back up the complete save set (your saves folder), not only the GDD. Keep the GDD, its recovery and snapshot directories, and the `course-*` files together.
Tracks that use the new wind or CPU aggression settings save a newer settings block that 1.2.x cannot read. Tracks that do not use them stay readable by older builds. Keep your backup if you might go back to 1.2.x.

## New: G-Diffuser Companion (Windows and Linux)

The Windows x64, Linux x64 and Linux arm64 downloads now include the Companion, a separate desktop program in the `companion` folder inside your G-Diffuser folder. It builds the files G-Diffuser loads and checks every input before it builds. It never edits your settings, saves or stores.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.3 - Course Editor Hotfix
releases.body:
## Fixes
- Correct complete-course snapshot content binding so metadata-only edits do not reuse an incompatible retained snapshot.
- Handle terminal disk-write refusals without trapping Course Edit in its save wait loop.
- Fix the host editor's remaining 64-node admission ceiling. The supported total remains 127 nodes, including forks.
- Restore Content Library layout previews for supported tracks above 64 nodes.
- Adapt native load, overwrite, and delete confirmations to long filenames while keeping normal-size text and the Yes/No controls in place.
- Size the Course Edit information panel dynamically to fit the track title, length, and node count.

## Save compatibility — read before updating
Close the game and back up the complete installation save/state set before updating, not only the cartridge `.sav` file.

This release writes version-2 `.gcs` snapshots and still reads version 1. Older builds cannot read version-2 snapshots or packages that contain them. Before downgrading, restore the complete matching pre-upgrade save/state backup. Keeping old snapshots alone is not sufficient.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.2 - Save and Import Hotfix
releases.body:
## G-Diffuser 1.2.2 - Save and Import Hotfix

- Fix disk-write ownership checks that could prevent Course Edit saves from completing and cause track imports to fail with MFS error 244.
- Preserve snapshot validation, rollback, and recovery protections during save and import operations.
- Add regression coverage using the production disk-write helper, including write failures and rollback.

Back up your installation's save and course-state files before updating. This hotfix does not change the course snapshot format.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.1 - The Small Improvements and Fixes Update
releases.body:
## Back up before upgrading

Close the game and back up the complete save set (your saves folder), not only the GDD. Keep the GDD, its recovery and snapshot directories, and `course-elements.gdxs`, `course-forks.gbs`, and
`course-settings.gks` together. Do not open snapshot-backed saves in an older executable.
The new, extended tracks that go above the original 64 node limit are not compatible with the original Expansion Kit or older tools.

## Course Edit

- Widen the native course information panel at a fixed size. Keep full 20-character names on
  one row and fit three-digit node counts without moving the buttons below it. Dynamic sizing
  is deferred.

- Raise the combined main-path and alternate-path control-point ceiling to **127**. Geometry,
  jump, effect, decoration, and junction budgets still apply; 127 points is not a guarantee
  that every layout fits.
- Add complete, content-bound save snapshots for extended courses and complete course/cup
  package sharing. Missing or mismatched required snapshot data is rejected rather than
  silently loading a truncated course.
- Keep both paths selectable after editor reload and save/reload. Show stored branch nodes

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.0 - The Big Upgrade Edition
releases.body:
1.2.0 brings G-Diffuser to macOS and Android, adds an in-game updater, and is the biggest Course Edit update so far: Mouse Controls, undo, forks, lava strips from F-Zero GX, Magnet strips for the original F-Zero, and Blender-style camera controls. Thanks to everyone in the feature requests channel who shaped it.

## Before you update

- **Coming from 1.1.0, download this release by hand.** 1.1.0 has no updater. From 1.2 on, desktop builds can update themselves.
- **To install by hand,** extract the release over your existing `G-Diffuser` folder. Your `saves/`, ROM and game data stay where they are.
- **Rebuild your ROM hack archives.** Hacks now carry more of their own data, and an archive built by an older version doesn't have it.
- **Continue Cup is per hack.** An existing `gp_resume.bin` stays with the stock game, and each hack starts with no saved cup.
- **Courses that use new features need 1.2.** Forks, magnet traps, custom music and custom elements are ignored or lost on older versions.
